summary: Built 'Rescan as administrator' as designed. A pure App file (RescanAsAdministrator.cs) holds Offers, WorthProbing, IsRescannableType, IsDriveRootShape, Start (runas, quoted root only, 1223 → declined line) and the injected-reader probe. A new Core.Native GlobalDosDevices (over a Kernel32 open of \\?\GLOBALROOT\GLOBAL??\X:\) keeps SUBST and mapped letters from being offered. MainWindow runs the probe on the scan task and sets the button before EndingShown, with the button and a status line on the pickers' line; WindowReport reads it as rescanAsAdministrator.offered plus a window key. The pre-modified fitness.yaml block was kept and widened per the accepted findings (family ban, manifest bans, call-site and hook rules). Builder-owned tests, two corpora and a stub-able window script replace the absent E005 files. Run for real unelevated on this PC, the script held end to end: the unelevated starts raised no prompt, and the whole-D: scan finished inside the 90 s bound and offered from a visible button in view. The UAC press itself cannot be driven here.

files.why: The pure offer decision, probe, press and wording (Offers, WorthProbing, IsRescannableType, IsDriveRootShape, Start, DriveTypeAnElevatedCopySees with injected readers).
Public facade HoldsDriveLetter(char): whether a drive letter is held by the global DOS-device namespace an elevated copy sees.
Internal OpensThroughGlobalDosDevices reusing OpenRootForQuery inside a CriticalErrorBoxOff; OpenRootForQuery's comment names the third caller.
The pickers' line becomes a DockPanel holding RescanAsAdministratorButton and the RescanStatus line, both collapsed until an ending offers; line stays one button tall.
Probe on the scan task, ShowOutcome sets the button before EndingShown, StartScan resets it, the one Click handler calls RescanAsAdministrator.Start; button text and tooltip set from the constants.
Additive schema-1 keys: top-level rescanAsAdministrator.offered and window RescanAsAdministratorButton {visible, enabled, inView}, both read from the button; remarks paragraph.
Kept the engine's SL-008 block and rewrote it per accepted M2, m3, m4: the elevation API-family ban, the manifest bans (src and root build files), the call-site rule and the hook rule.
Rule and ReadRule made internal so the new corpus test reads fitness entries by the same reader.
Every Offers branch, each ScanStatus, DriveType, root spelling with its expected value, and the WorthProbing/IsRescannableType/IsDriveRootShape pin (M1, m5).

Probe: system drive vs SubstDrive letter (== IsSystem, m1), injected network/CDRom/Ram/NoRootDirectory/Unknown types never open the namespace, throwing readers give null, every rescannable type gives null for a letter the namespace lacks (m5).

Start: every A:\..Z:\ and a:\..z:\ with a spaced exe path splits to exactly [root] through CommandLineToArgvW and CommandLine; 1223 → DeclinedLine; codes 2/5/1155/others → refused line; null/empty exe; crafted non-drive roots refused; process disposed.
Behavioural fact on MainWindow.xaml.cs (M2): Start called once inside the handler's body, handler named nowhere else, no ClickEvent/RaiseEvent/automation invoke, no using static or alias.
Class corpus for the elevation rules (m3, m4, M2): 56 fire/quiet rows with a 'before' column computed from the design's own patterns.
Runs the corpus against the fitness.yaml patterns, recomputes the before column, and runs the rules over the real tree.
Runs every ending row of the window script through -Stub under pwsh and Windows PowerShell 5.1, the pre-fix table (mutant copy) for the before column, and one scenario per exit code (m2, M1).

The unattended exe-level check: privileged INCONCLUSIVE row, case 13 short runs by CreateProcess (740/timeout/no report FAILED), folder and root-unreadable negatives, global-letter drive pick, positive drive run, combination rule, -Stub.
Ending-table class corpus (m2): 44 stubbed scenarios with expect, steps and the pre-fix 'before' exit code.
Producers row for the new script, which names the exe and doubles trailing backslashes.

obligations.how: RescanAsAdministratorOfferTests.AFinishedScanOfAFixedOrRemovableDriveThatLeftFoldersUnreadOffersIt feeds C:\, c:\, Z:\, z:\, E:\, e:\ and the \\?\ spellings with Fixed/Removable and unreadable 1, 5000: passes.

OnlyAScanThatCompletedOffersIt runs every ScanStatus value (Cancelled, RootUnreadable, Refused included): only Completed offers. ShowOutcome's early returns and ShowProblem leave the button as StartScan collapsed it.

ARootIsADriveOnlyInTheShapeOfOne gives the expected value for each spelling (true for C:\, c:\, \\?\C:\; false for C:, folders with and without backslash, \\server\share, \\?\UNC\...). The report half (key present, offered false) runs for real in the script's folder, folder-slash and root-unreadable steps. A UNC share could not be made unattended, so the report side of UNC is not run at exe level.
ADriveThatWasReadInFullDoesNotOfferIt: unreadable 0 and -1 never offer, 1 and int.MaxValue do. Script rows D05/D06 cover it at the report.

ATypeThatIsNotLocalIsReturnedAsItIsAndTheNamespaceIsNeverAsked: injected Network, CDRom, Ram, NoRootDirectory, Unknown are returned unchanged, holdsLetter is never called, and Offers refuses them. No test touches Z:\ (lesson #878).

TheProbeGivesTheSystemDriveItsTypeAndASubstLetterNone: system drive gives its type, a SubstDrive letter gives null (Fixed under SYSTEM, per m1); ASubstLetterIsGlobalOnlyWhenSubstMadeItInTheGlobalNamespace asserts HoldsDriveLetter == IsSystem. Measured here: a SUBST letter reads as DriveType Fixed, so only the namespace open refuses it.
AReadThatThrowsAnIoAccessOrArgumentExceptionGivesNull: IOException, UnauthorizedAccessException, ArgumentException and subclasses from either the type read or the namespace read give null.
AnElevatedCopyNeverOffersItWhateverElseHolds: elevated true never offers for any DriveType. Offers and the probe gate share WorthProbing.

EveryDriveRootReachesTheNewCopyAsItsOneArgumentAndNothingElse (52 rows, A:\..Z:\ and a:\..z:\, exe path with spaces): FileName is the exe, ArgumentList empty, no --report, CommandLineToArgvW split is exactly [root], CommandLine.Arguments leaves it unchanged and RootArgument returns the root.

ADeclinedPromptIsTheDeclinedLineAndWindowsIsCalledOnce: Win32Exception 1223 gives DeclinedLine, Windows called once. Declare-only: a real prompt cannot be driven (lesson #24, and the engine treats a raised prompt as misuse).

AnyOtherRefusalIsTheRefusedLineWithItsCodeAndNoPath (2, 5, 1155, 740, 1, 1222, 1224, 0) and NoProgramFileIsTheNoProgramLineAndWindowsIsNeverCalled (null, empty): lines say 'was not started', ASCII, no exe path or root.

tests/window/SL-008-RescanOfferOnALocalDrive.Tests.ps1 run for real unelevated: it picked D: (the Fixed drive with least used space, 230 GB, global letter); the scan finished inside the 90 s bound I put on it, with 2 folders unread, and the report read offered true from a visible button in view with PickerPanel's height equal to the folder run's. Exit 0, ALL CHECKS HELD. A full-bound (3600 s) run is the engine's command.

The same script's no-path, path-window and folder-report steps start the exe by CreateProcess from an unelevated shell: still up after 6 s with no prompt, and report runs end exit 0; 740, timeout and no report are FAILED (rows S01-S07 prove each). Real run: all held.

Built the builder-owned tests M1 asks for instead of the absent E005 files: RescanAsAdministratorOfferTests (every Offers branch with the critic's per-root expectations), 1223 in RescanAsAdministratorStartTests, and the no-offer report negatives (folder, folder with backslash, root-unreadable: key present, offered false) in the SL-008 script. Case 13 got its own short CreateProcess runs before the drive scan (740, timeout, no report FAILED) with the combination rule any FAILED > any INCONCLUSIVE; the stopped-scan negative is dropped as the critic said.

Three layers: the fitness entry banning RescanAsAdministrator.Start, OnRescanAsAdministrator, 'using static' and alias spellings outside MainWindow.xaml.cs and the rescan file; the hook entry banning 'rescan as admin' in any case under tests/window/FsaWindowHook/**; and RescanElevationGuardTests (Start once inside the handler's body, handler named once plus the XAML Click=, no ClickEvent/RaiseEvent/AutomationPeer/IInvokeProvider/InvokePattern, no OnLoaded/StartScan/ShowOutcome/ShowProblem/AddVolumeInUse call, App.xaml.cs/WindowReport.cs/ReportFile.cs clean). Verified: a second Start call in ShowOutcome turns the first fact red.

The SUBST assertions state the namespace rule: HoldsDriveLetter(subst) == WindowsIdentity.GetCurrent().IsSystem, and the probe gives Fixed under SYSTEM and null otherwise; the system-drive half is unconditional.

Script: privilege read by WindowsPrincipal.IsInRole(Administrator) or IsSystem (works under 5.1 and 7) taken before any launch (INCONCLUSIVE exit 2); drive picked only when it opens through GLOBAL?? from the script, QueryDosDevice alternative dropped; -Stub replaces launch, report read, privilege and drive list; combination rule any FAILED > INCONCLUSIVE. Corpus of 44 rows (M01-M04 are the class members). RescanOfferEndingsTests runs every row under pwsh and Windows PowerShell 5.1, and a copy of the script with the two MUTATE lines removed (the table before the fix) fails M01, M02, M03, M04 with exit 1 where the fix gives 2/2/0/2.

The verb pattern is replaced by the family ban outside RescanAsAdministrator.cs: runas, lpVerb, UseShellExecute, ShellExecute\w*, Elevation:Administrator; reflection on ProcessStartInfo is named as uncaught in the entry's because and in the corpus. 56-row corpus; RescanElevationRulesCorpusTests recomputes the design's own patterns as the 'before' column: 22+ rows were quiet and now fire (Verb ??=, Verb +=, a verb built as two strings, the shell entry points, the COM moniker) and 4 over-broad matches (Verb =>, const Verb) are lifted.

Two entries ban (?m)\b(ApplicationManifest|Win32Manifest|Win32Resource)\b: over src/** (App csproj, any src Directory.Build.* at any depth) and over Directory.Build.* at the repo root; the start rule keeps requireAdministrator/highestAvailable over src/FsAnalyser.App/**. Corpus rows C01-C06 and D01-D03; the tree is clean under them. The behavioural guard is case 13's CreateProcess short run.

RescanAsAdministrator.WorthProbing(status, unreadable, elevated), IsRescannableType(DriveType) and IsDriveRootShape(string) are each written once; the scan task's lambda calls WorthProbing, Offers starts with it and calls the other two, and the probe runs the namespace open exactly when IsRescannableType holds. OffersIsFalseWheneverWorthProbingIsFalseAndIsNothingMoreThanItsThreeQuestions sweeps every combination (>500 rows); ForEveryRescannableTypeALetterTheNamespaceDoesNotHoldGivesNull pins the probe.

13 passed: the 44-row ending corpus under pwsh and Windows PowerShell 5.1, the pre-fix table (mutant) failing M01-M04, exit codes 0/1/2, and the producers row.

Real, unelevated, published app on this PC (publish step ran). no-path and path-window: window stayed up, no prompt. folder, folder-slash, root-unreadable: key present and false. drive-pick: D: (230 GB used, global letter). drive: the scan finished inside 90 s with 2 folders unread and offered=true read from a visible, in-view button with PickerPanel's height unchanged. Exit 0.

1635 tests. 1 of 4 runs passed all 1635. The other 3 failed only UnfinishedTests.StopsInTheSizeChecksMarkWhatAPendingCheckCouldChange(workers: 4), a stop-timing test in Core scanning this slice does not touch; it passes alone (6/6). With my three new test classes filtered out, 3 further runs also failed it, plus CancellationTests on the unreachable share and a CloudPlaceholderTests stall test, so the flake is the PC's current load and network state and predates this slice.

tests.note: All 7 mutations turned their named test red (e.g. 16 of 19 rows for the Offers shape mutation, the guard fact for a second Start call); the tree was restored after each (git status clean of mutations).

tests.note: Six captures came back all black: no visible desktop for this session. Layout is judged from the report's inView and PickerPanel height keys, not from a picture.

deviations: Start also refuses a root that is not a whole-drive shape (NotADriveLine, Windows never called), which the design did not say. Reason: the command line goes to an elevated copy, and lesson #914 asks for crafted roots; a root carrying a quote, --report or a second argument can never reach it. It costs one branch, tested with folders, shares, bare letters and injection-shaped roots.

The design's case 13 and the planted E005 scripts are replaced as accepted finding M1 says: the SL-008 script owns case 13 as its own short CreateProcess runs before the drive scan (740, timeout and no report are FAILED), the stopped-scan negative is dropped, and the combination rule is any FAILED > any INCONCLUSIVE. UNC-share report negatives are not run at exe level (no share can be made unattended); the Offers tests cover the \\server and \\?\UNC\ spellings.

The engine-appended SL-008 fitness block was rewritten, not kept as it came: the Verb pattern became the elevation API-family ban (m3), manifest bans were added over src/** and root Directory.Build.* (m4), a call-site entry and a hook entry were added (M2), and the call-site pattern tolerates whitespace and line breaks around the dot.

The button's text and tooltip are set in MainWindow's constructor from RescanAsAdministrator's constants rather than written in the XAML, so the words are written once and the linked tests see the same ones.
SettledRulesCorpusTests.Rule and ReadRule were made internal so the new corpus test reads fitness entries by the same reader instead of a second YAML reader.

No Settings checkbox or notice was built for the GLOBAL?? letter gate, as the design decided: Windows keeps a separate DOS-device map per logon session by design (it is documented, with EnableLinkedConnections as its own workaround), and the gate only withholds an offer that would end as 'Could not read'. I considered the standing one-checkbox-per-outside-defect rule against that decision and kept the design; a reviewer who reads it as an outside defect should say so.
not_built: The press itself end to end (UAC prompt, elevated copy scanning the same root): cannot be driven unattended, and the engine treats a raised prompt as misuse. Start is proved through the injected start function; finish line 6 stays the person's check on a UAC-on PC.
A test of 'start another scan after an offered ending' (case 14): not material in the design; the reset is HideRescanOffer beside StartScan's other Hide* resets, left for code review.
A picture of the offered ending: the screen capture is black in this session. The report's inView and PickerPanel height keys are the layout evidence.
SeBackupPrivilege, an elevated helper, IPC and merging into the open scan: left out on purpose, as the design's over_engineering_flag says.
follow_ups: Editing MainWindow, WindowReport and Core.Native makes the person's network, C:\ and OneDrive proof runs stale under the project's staleness lists; Q-016 already orders them after E-005, E-006 and E-007.

RescanAsAdministrator.IsDriveRootShape restates Core's internal VolumeSpace.IsDriveRoot. Exposing one public shape test from Core would remove the second copy; this slice kept to the design's restatement.

UnfinishedTests.StopsInTheSizeChecksMarkWhatAPendingCheckCouldChange(workers: 4) failed in 3 of 4 full runs here, and CancellationTests and a cloud stall test fail under this PC's load with my classes excluded. It deserves its own look; this slice did not touch scanning.
Q-002 (outcome texts capped at 76 px) is still open; the offer sits on the pickers' line to stay out of it, so it does not need Q-002 answered.

The RescanStatus line is trimmed with a tooltip at the 560 px minimum width (about 60 px of room beside the three buttons); a later slice could move the started/declined line if that proves too short in use.
